_contract.scenario: addItem below availability → pendingConfirmation(belowAtp) → the same requestId + confirmToken commits, stamping the fraud flag

data._note: header / lines / totals are UNCHANGED — version has not moved. Elided here; see 02.

_notes: The SAME requestId spans both calls — one user action. The confirmToken is what changes.
The token IS the audit record: it proves the agent was shown available:2 before accepting. A client-set boolean could not prove that (map note 8, ticket 136 Q4).
ATP is a SOFT gate — the commit always succeeds. 287's rule survives: where the stock read degrades (known:false) there is no confirmation step at all.
atpAtScan stays frozen at 2 (availability at add), not 5 (requested) — the BackOffice fraud signal 285/286 reads this pair.
A stale token (basket moved underneath) returns CONFIRM_TOKEN_STALE and the client re-asks without a token.
